mentions.name: ffl
mentions.description: A single-binary file transfer tool built as an Actually Portable Executable (APE) on Cosmopolitan Libc. It turns any file or folder into a secure peer-to-peer HTTPS link via WebRTC, letting users share files with one command across platforms (demoed round-trip transfer between Windows x64 and Android arm64 with the same binary).
mentions.problem: Moving large files (logs, DB dumps) in and out of containers was painful; this tool reduces it to a single command.
mentions.source_excerpt: I'm working on ffl (https://github.com/nuwainfo/ffl), an Actually Portable Executable (APE) that turns any file or folder into a secure P2P HTTPS link via WebRTC.

mentions.name: FastFileLink
mentions.description: A file-sharing CLI and app that uses WebRTC for P2P transfer while exposing HTTPS links, making it compatible with browsers and tools like curl/wget. For huge files it supports resumable upload to an infra-backed server with fast global downloads, and the CLI will also support receiving files via WebRTC. It is open source and used to move files between containers and hosts.
mentions.problem: Moving files between containers and hosts is awkward when volumes aren't mounted, and exchanging large files remotely typically requires a relay server.
mentions.audience: Internal users moving files between containers and hosts, and WFH employees exchanging large files
mentions.source_excerpt: I am working on FastFileLink (https://fastfilelink.com/), yet another file-sharing CLI/app that uses WebRTC for P2P transfer but exposes HTTPS links, making it compatible with browsers and tools like curl/wget.
